complexity.explanation: Matrix transformations manipulate the 3x3 affine transformation matrix in 2D graphics state memory. Pushing state, translating, rotating, and drawing primitive bounds operates in constant O(1) time with minimal stack allocation.

executionTrace.memoryDetail: Pushes a copy of the current 3x3 Current Transformation Matrix (CTM) and clipping path onto the graphics state stack.
Pre-multiplies CTM by translation matrix [[1, 0, cx], [0, 1, cy], [0, 0, 1]], shifting local (0, 0) to canvas center (150, 150).
Pre-multiplies CTM by 45° rotation matrix [[cos θ, -sin θ, 0], [sin θ, cos θ, 0], [0, 0, 1]], establishing a rotated local coordinate space.
Rasterizes an 80x80 rectangle symmetrically centered around local origin (-40, -40 to +40, +40), creating a centered rotation.
Pops and restores the original transformation matrix, isolating transforms from subsequent draw passes.

pitfalls.title: Missing ctx.save / ctx.restore Matrix Leaks
pitfalls.description: Failing to bracket canvas coordinate mutations with save() and restore() causes transformations to accumulate across animation frames or bleed into subsequent rendering passes.

pitfalls.title: Rotating Before Translating Sweeps Local Axes
pitfalls.description: Matrix multiplications are non-commutative (A · B ≠ B · A). Calling rotate() before translate() rotates the axis vectors first, causing translate() to advance along angled directions and swing the shape around world (0, 0).

seniorInterviewTip: Move the paper under the pen, not the pen across the paper. In Canvas and GPU rendering, coordinate transforms do not move shapes; they transform the coordinate space itself. Senior engineers always translate the origin to the object's anchor or center of mass before rotating or scaling.
